title: Mt. Carmel Session v. New Jersey Presbytery
disposition_detail: General Assembly defeated the minority report, adopted the SJC majority report, and denied the complaint.
first_summary: Mt. Carmel Session challenged New Jersey Presbytery's creation-days resolution, arguing that the Westminster Standards require six consecutive twenty-four-hour days. The SJC majority concluded that Presbytery could resolve the doctrinal question under BCO 11-4 and that prior Assembly actions permitted latitude on the length of the creation days. The General Assembly rejected the minority report, adopted the majority report, and denied the complaint.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The SJC case was referred because nine members filed a minority report; the 26th Assembly defeated that report and adopted the majority.
evidence_notes.dispute: Mt. Carmel Session contended that New Jersey Presbytery's creation-days resolution contradicted the Westminster Standards.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The majority denied the complaint, reasoning that BCO 11-4 permitted Presbytery to resolve the doctrinal question and prior Assembly actions allowed interpretive latitude; the Assembly made that result final.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The minority argued for the twenty-four-hour-day reading, but its report was defeated and is not the holding.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Prior Assembly creation-days actions are discussed as supporting context, not substituted for the operative Case 97-5 judgment.

source_limits: The full minutes preserve the majority and minority materials and the final Assembly action; vote-registration details do not alter the operative disposition.
